_meta.indication: IMJUDO, in combination with durvalumab, is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multicenter, global comparative trial evaluating tremelimumab plus durvalumab (T300+D), durvalumab monotherapy, and sorafenib.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with previously untreated, unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS) superiority of T300+D versus sorafenib.
pivotal_trials.n: N=1171 randomized in the analysis population; T300+D 393, durvalumab 389, sorafenib 389.
pivotal_trials.result: T300+D showed statistically significant OS improvement versus sorafenib: median OS 16.4 vs 13.8 months; HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.66, 0.92); 2-sided p=0.0035.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) in uHCC were rash, diarrhea, fatigue, pruritus, musculoskeletal pain, and abdominal pain. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 41% of patients; fatal adverse reactions occurred in 8%.
target_moa: Tremelimumab is a CTLA-4 blocking antibody that binds CTLA-4 and blocks its interaction with ligands CD80 and CD86, releasing CTLA-4-mediated inhibition of T-cell activation.

rems.type: A REMS was determined not to be required to ensure safe and effective use of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee (ODAC) as no significant review issues were identified.

basis.text: FDA advised against formal submission of a Breakthrough Therapy Designation Request as the data did not demonstrate a substantial improvement over available therapy.

citations.quote: Preliminary Breakthrough Therapy Designation Request Meeting on November 10, 2021FDA advised against formal submission of a BTDR as the data submitted to support BTD did not demonstrate a substantial improvement over available therapy.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation was granted on 15 January 2020 to tremelimumab for the treatment of HCC.

citations.quote: In addition, Orphan Drug Designation was granted on 15 January 2020 to durvalumab and tremelimumab for the treatment of HCC (19-7215 and 19-7214, respectively).

summary.text: BLA 761289 for tremelimumab (IMJUDO) received Priority review and was supported by the pivotal HIMALAYA trial; tremelimumab had Orphan Drug Designation for HCC. It was a traditional (not accelerated) approval, with no Breakthrough Therapy Designation granted.

citations.quote: In addition, Orphan Drug Designation was granted on 15 January 2020 to durvalumab and tremelimumab for the treatment of HCC (19-7215 and 19-7214, respectively).
The effectiveness of tremelimumab and durvalumab for the proposed indication was established in study HIMALAYA (pivotal trial).

requirement.text: 4333-1: Conduct Study D419EC00001, a Phase I/II open-label study to evaluate safety, PK, and preliminary efficacy of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in pediatric patients from birth to <18 years with relapsed/refractory malignant solid tumors or hematological malignancy.

citations.quote: 4333-1 Conduct Study D419EC00001 (A Phase I/II, open-label, multicenter study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in pediatric patients) to further characterize the safety, pharmacokinetics, and efficacy of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in patients from birth to <18 years of age with relapsed/refractory malignant solid tumors or a relapsed/refractory hematological malignancy including lymphomas for whom no standard treatment is available. Include at least 12 patients in the dose escalation cohort and at least 45 evaluable patients in the dose expansion cohort.

requirement.text: 4333-2: Conduct Study 2 to evaluate efficacy and safety of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in children from birth to <18 years with a pediatric solid tumor.

citations.quote: 4333-2 Conduct a study, Study 2, to evaluate the efficacy and safety of tremelimumab used in combination with durvalumab in children from birth to less than 18 years of age with a pediatric solid tumor, to further characterize the efficacy and safety of tremelimumab in combination with durvalumab in pediatric solid tumors.

requirement.text: 4333-4: Perform a shipping validation study under real-time shipping conditions using a representative commercial tremelimumab drug product lot.

citations.quote: 4333-4 To perform a shipping validation study under real time shipping conditions (i.e., temperature, mode of transport, shipping duration, and shipping containers and packing representative of the minimum and maximum load) using a representative commercial tremelimumab drug product lot in the final commercial container closure and packaging systems to evaluate the ability of the shipping containers to maintain the recommended temperature and to evaluate the impact of shipping from the AstraZeneca Sweden labeling and packaging site to the US Distribution Center on the physical integrity and product quality of tremelimumab drug product. The shipping validation data will be submitted in accordance with 21 CFR 601.12.
